clue.text: Boring way of discovering success and wealth

definitions.text: Boring way of discovering success and wealth

parts.words: Boring way of discovering success and wealth
parts.note: boring here means drilling into the ground, and a drill that finds petroleum also stands for a sudden windfall

explanation.surface: A dull, plodding route to getting rich and successful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as 'dull', but it is drilling: a well that finds petroleum is the literal sense, and sudden fortune the figurative one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a sudden lucky fortune comes from prospectors drilling a well and hitting a gusher of petroleum.

clue.text: Many yarns have been spun about it

definitions.text: Many yarns have been spun about it

parts.words: Many yarns have been spun about it
parts.note: yarns suggests tall stories told about something, but literally thread is spun around a rod on a spinning wheel

explanation.surface: A subject that has inspired countless tall tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarns' and 'spun' look like storytelling; read literally, they describe thread wound round the rod of a spinning wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender rod on a spinning wheel or machine onto which thread is twisted and wound.

clue.text: During the interval is to oppose

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of another, so the word is goes inside

parts.note: a rest is an interval or pause, as in music

explanation.surface: A break in proceedings is the moment to put up opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand or fight against something is to stand against it.

clue.text: Leave the light off when one has to conceal something

explanation.surface: Switch off the lamp when you have a secret to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally, keeping a room unlit; idiomatically, keeping something secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means not switching on a lamp; as an idiom it means keeping a matter secret and telling nobody.

clue.text: Leo north came up at the present time

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the name taken as written; that Leo and the N of north sit side by side in the clue is a coincidence, not a hidden run

explanation.surface: A man called Leo travelled north just now.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read LEON as a hidden run, but no word signals hiding: it is LEO plus N for north, and 'came up' turns the lot. 'The present time' is the season of gifts, not 'now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the season when gifts are given, punningly the time for presents.

clue.text: Barely beat one's opponents?

parts.note: barely suggests only just winning, but read as naked it pictures shedding clothes in the open air

explanation.surface: Win by the narrowest of margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' means 'only just' on the surface; cryptically it means 'naked', so the word splits as 'out' plus 'strip'.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or outrun others, while its two halves suggest undressing outdoors.

clue.text: Design etched on floor-covering first

indicators.note: on places the etched piece after the floor-covering piece in the answer
first confirms the floor-covering piece comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: lino is short for linoleum, a floor covering
etched means carved or cut into a surface

explanation.surface: A pattern scratched into the flooring before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A print or picture made from a pattern carved into a block of linoleum.

clue.text: Article left out of treatise rewritten in port

indicators.note: rewritten says the remaining letters are put into a new order
left out of means the article's letter is dropped from the word treatise

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammatical article omitted from a scholarly essay, which is then revised in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of' removes A from TREATISE, leaving TRETISE, which 'rewritten' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian city and harbour at the head of the Adriatic.

clue.text: One who takes the long view

definitions.text: One who takes the long view

parts.words: One who takes the long view
parts.note: taking the long view usually means planning ahead, but here it is literally looking at distant objects through an instrument

explanation.surface: Someone who thinks far into the future.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for forward planning is read literally: someone who looks a long way through an optical tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who uses an optical instrument to observe distant objects such as stars.

clue.text: Friendly understanding that could be more than cordial

definitions.text: Friendly understanding that could be more than cordial

parts.words: Friendly understanding that could be more than cordial
parts.note: the 1904 Anglo-French agreement was called cordiale, so the word could stand with more than that adjective

explanation.surface: An amicable agreement that might be warmer than merely polite.
explanation.walkthrough: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 Anglo-French agreement; the answer is a friendly understanding, with or without 'cordial' after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly agreement or informal alliance between nations, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Green on the same side is not threatening the environment

parts.note: eco- is the prefix for green or environmental matters
people on the same side are allies, friendly to one another

explanation.surface: A Green ally poses no danger to nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the definition, but it supplies only the prefix ECO.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing products or practices that do no harm to nature.

clue.text: Title had initially been put in ramshackle display

indicators.note: put in places the single letter inside the reworked letters
something ramshackle is falling apart, so the letters of display are jumbled
initially picks the opening letter of the word had

explanation.surface: A heading has been inserted into a rickety exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramshackle' rearranges DISPLAY, and 'initially' takes H from 'had', which 'put in' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of address for a woman of noble rank, such as a peeress or a lord's wife.

clue.text: Various cuts made by commander on plaster

indicators.note: various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of cuts are rearranged

parts.note: CO stands for commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer making several incisions in a wall's plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plaster' looks like a verb going with 'cuts', but it is the noun and the definition; 'made by' and 'on' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine plaster used to coat walls or mould decorations.

clue.text: Get men in to vandalise plant!

indicators.note: vandalise means wreck or break up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Bring in workers to wreck a factory!
explanation.walkthrough: 'to vandalise' looks like the purpose of the men; 'to' is part of the fodder, and 'plant' is a flower, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden annual with fragrant small flowers, grown as an ornamental.

clue.text: Look out for said believer

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a Sikh is a believer in Sikhism

explanation.surface: Be on the lookout for someone who is reported to be religious.
explanation.definitionFit: To search for or try to find something.

clue.text: Dispense these days with one in church

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a minister serves in a church

explanation.surface: Get rid of modern habits along with a churchgoer.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out or deal something, such as medicine or justice.

clue.text: Softie travelling about freezing-point in a type of skiing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
travelling moves the letters about, so softie is rearranged

parts.note: FP is an abbreviation for freezing point

explanation.surface: A weakling on holiday, worried about the cold, on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges SOFTIE, which goes 'about' FP.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing on unprepared snow away from the groomed runs.

clue.text: Taken from photo no longer obtainable from publisher

explanation.surface: A picture lifted from a photograph that can no longer be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally, cut from a photographic print; idiomatically, a book no longer published.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic print is a photo, so something cut from one is taken from it; a book is unavailable once the publisher stops producing it.

clue.text: Get rid of grass in the pavilion

parts.note: turf is grass with its roots
in cricket a dismissed batsman goes back to the pavilion, so is out

explanation.surface: Clear the lawn from inside the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the pavilion is the clubhouse; a batsman back there has been dismissed, or 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrasal verb meaning expel or throw someone out.

clue.text: Spots bill, one without the ball

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: without means the round letter is taken out of the word one

parts.note: O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped a bill and has no ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes O, shaped like a ball, from ONE, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition marked by pimples on the face.

clue.text: Tribe surrounding city had old trumpet

indicators.note: surrounding means the tribe's letters go round the city

parts.note: a clan is a tribe or family group
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, is usually called Rio

explanation.surface: A people encircling a town once owned a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill medieval war trumpet, now used figuratively for a rousing call.

clue.text: Diminutive lady going over the edge with vertigo

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means placed above, so the lady comes first

parts.note: Meg is a short form of the name Margaret
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A tiny woman suffers dizziness as she topples off the brink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive' suggests a small woman, but means a pet form of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for dizziness or a migraine headache.

clue.text: Break in to repair rupture located within

indicators.note: located within says the letters are found inside the words repair rupture

explanation.surface: Burst in to fix an inner rupture.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst or rush suddenly into a place.

clue.text: Eccentric named Ron having been sent back into custody

definitions.text: having been sent back into custody

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd character called Ron is returned to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: In British law a defendant on remand is held in custody until trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal phrase for a defendant held in prison awaiting trial.

clue.text: Heather loses a man

indicators.note: loses means the letter a is dropped

parts.note: Erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather loses a male friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a woman's name, but it is the plant, whose Latin name is the genus Erica.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, so any male person in crossword terms.

clue.text: Press used on only half a garment?

definitions.text: Press used on only half a garment?

parts.words: Press used on only half a garment?
parts.note: a pressing device for ... is named with the singular, as if it pressed just one leg of the pair

explanation.surface: An iron applied to just one side of a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The trouser press is named in the singular, as if for one leg of a pair of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: The singular form names one leg of a pair of slacks, and is used in compounds like the pressing device.

clue.text: Dilatory perhaps, nothing missing lately

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible arrangement, so the remaining letters are reworked
missing means the zero letter is taken out of the word dilatory

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Slow, maybe, with nothing absent recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes O from DILATORY, leaving DILATRY, which 'perhaps' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Done late or behind schedule; tardily and lately both mean in a late way.

clue.text: Would digging give him a healthy appetite?

definitions.text: Would digging give him a healthy appetite?

parts.words: Would digging give him a healthy appetite?
parts.note: a man who digs ditches might be called a ditch man, and a trencher is also an old wooden plate

explanation.surface: Does working in the garden make a man hungry?
explanation.walkthrough: A trencher was a wooden plate, so a hearty eater is named for it; the clue reads it as a man who digs trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats heartily, named after the old wooden platter.
